title: Starter Bento Playbook: LLM Integration Lab
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, transportable playbook for engineers who need a minimal, repeatable path to integrate an LLM-powered feature using Redwood’s SDKs. Treat as a lab recipe: opinionated defaults, runnable in ~20 minutes, and easy to fork.

Audience / Personas:
- Product engineers building a first Prodigy or chat feature
- Platform engineers evaluating the Redwood client for internal self-serve
- Solutions engineers preparing a demo for a customer POC

Non-goals:
- Full security / enterprise deployment guide (see private-deployments docs)
- Deep performance tuning (serving-runtime team owns advanced guides)

High-level flow (one-pager):
1) Boot a small local dev env (docker-compose) with local mock network
2) Install the minimal client (JS or Py) and wire an API key with scoped demo creds
3) Run the quickstart example (generation + streaming + error fallback)
4) Hook in telemetry (token cost + latency); show Console route view
5) Add one prebuilt prompt template + simple eval test (unit test style)
6) Iterate: swap in a quantized model variant and show fallback behavior

Opinionated defaults (why):
- Model: use redwood-inference/llama-4b-compact for quick latency/cost tradeoff (good demo economics)
- Streaming: enable by default to highlight UX advantages
- Retry policy: 2 retries, exponential backoff starting at 200ms (keeps demo snappy)
- Telemetry: send minimal event (route, model, tokens_used, latency_ms) to local collector

Quickstart (JS) - commands to run locally:
- git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/example-apps.git
- cd example-apps/bento-starter && cp .env.example .env
- # in .env set REDWOOD_API_KEY=demo-XXXX and REDWOOD_REGION=us-west1
- docker-compose up --build -d # brings up local dev server + telemetry collector
- npm ci && npm run dev:quickstart

Quickstart (Py) - minimal script snippet (paste into app.py):
- from redwood import RedwoodClient
- client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
- resp = client.generate(model='llama-4b-compact', prompt='Summarize this email in 2 lines')
- print(resp.text)

Error modes to demo (short notes):
- API quota exhaustion: client returns 429 -> show circuit-breaker UI and fallback to smaller model variant
- Token budget spike: telemetry alerts with token burn -> rollback example to smaller sequence length + caching
- Network flaps (mock by toggling container): client should stream partial content then resume; show graceful UI state

Observability hooks (how to show Console value quickly):
- Emit a single JSON line per request to the local collector: {route, model, tokens, latency_ms, status}
- Wire collector forwarder to a temporary Console Demo route (instructions in linked artifacts)
- Example Grafana dashboard (screenshot text included in the repo)

Prompt template + tiny eval (example):
- Template: "TL;DR: {{email_body}} -> 2-line summary"
- Eval: 5 curated emails, assert bot produces <= 2 lines and includes key phrase from each input
- Put eval as pytest unit and run in CI to show regression protection

Rollout & gating for a 1-week POC:
Day 0: fork repo, run quickstart locally
Day 1: add telemetry + run smoke tests (eval + latency checks)
Day 2-3: integrate into staging app, enable canary (10% traffic)
Day 4: observe token burn + errors, iterate prompt or enable caching
Day 5-7: prepare handoff doc + sample SLOs for Dedicated path if customer needs scale

Checklist before demo (quick):
- [ ] Repo forked and .env configured
- [ ] Local telemetry visible in collector
- [ ] Streaming enabled and tested across slow network
- [ ] Eval tests pass locally
- [ ] Snippets for Console view captured (route, tokens, latency)

Open questions / decisions (notes to self):
- Do we include a full OAuth flow for multi-user demos or stick to API-key demo only? (ask security team)
- Should the playbook recommend embedding caching by default for summarization workloads? (engagement with Optimize)
- Which sample model list should be the canonical default for demos across regions?

Notes / shortcuts for presenters:
- Use the "cost meter" overlay when demonstrating token burn (it’s in the telemetry collector UI)
- If network demo needs to look bad fast: run `tc qdisc` container helper to add 400ms latency
- Keep the demo input short to stay within free credits
